description: TT Media Server (Python) - request latency, pipeline stages, image-generation stage breakdown (denoising / VAE decode / conditioning), multihost video-gen breakdown, and per-process infrastructure. Transient asset; sunsets with the Python server (~4 months).

panels.description: Total HTTP requests/sec hitting the FastAPI server (auto-instrumented).
panels.title: Request Rate

panels.description: Generation jobs currently being processed by the model service (post-queue, pre-response). Reflects true model concurrency, unlike the HTTP in-flight gauge which only sees the ~2ms queue-and-202 handler.
panels.title: Jobs In Flight (model)

panels.description: 5xx error ratio over the last 5m. Alert threshold: 5%.
panels.title: Error Rate (5xx)

panels.description: End-to-end p99 request latency (FastAPI auto-instrumented).
panels.title: HTTP p99 Latency

panels.description: p50/p95/p99 of total request duration, grouped by model_type. Filter via the $model_type variable to focus on a single runner (e.g. sp_runner for video gen).
panels.title: End-to-End Latency Quantiles

panels.description: Successful requests/sec per model_type from the custom telemetry counter.
panels.title: Requests / sec per model_type
Pipeline Stages (where time is spent inside a request)

panels.description: p95 latency of each pipeline stage stacked. Lets you see which stage dominates request time.
panels.title: Pipeline Stage p95 (stacked)

panels.description: Completed denoising steps per second across all image models. This is the core generation capacity number: it moves with resolution, step count and batching.
panels.title: Denoising Throughput (steps/s)

panels.description: Images per second converted from latents to pixels by the VAE. Compare against denoising throughput: if this is the lower number, reconstruction is the limiter, not denoising.
panels.title: VAE Decode (images/s)

panels.description: Megapixels per second out of the VAE. Resolution-independent view of reconstruction capacity - images/s alone makes a 512x512 model look faster than a 1024x1024 one at equal silicon cost.
panels.title: VAE Decode (megapixels/s)

panels.description: Conditioning encode time as a share of total engine time. High values mean prompt encoding - not denoising - dominates, which is the usual signature of short/low-step image requests.
panels.title: Conditioning % of Engine Time

panels.description: Denoising steps/s split by resolution and batch size. Doubling resolution should cut steps/s; batching should raise it. If batching does not raise it, the batch is not being formed.
panels.title: Denoising steps/s by resolution & batch

panels.description: Denoising steps/s split by device and sampler. Divergence between devices running the same model and sampler is a per-host problem; divergence between samplers is expected.
panels.title: Denoising steps/s by device & sampler

panels.description: Per-step denoising latency, p50 and p99, by resolution and batch. The reciprocal of p50 is the per-device step rate; a widening p50-p99 gap means some steps are stalling.
panels.title: Denoising step latency p50 / p99

panels.description: Heatmap of per-step denoising latency. Each row is a bucket; intensity = count. Shows bimodal step timing (e.g. first step paying a compile or cache cost) that quantiles hide.
panels.title: Denoising step latency heatmap

panels.description: VAE decode throughput per resolution and batch, in images/s and megapixels/s. Flat images/s while denoising steps/s climbs means the VAE has become the bottleneck.
panels.title: VAE decode throughput (images/s & MP/s)

panels.description: VAE decode latency p50/p99 per resolution and batch. Rising with batch means the decode is not amortising across the batch.
panels.title: VAE decode latency p50 / p99

panels.description: Conditioning encode time per request, p50 and p99, in milliseconds. 'all' is the pipeline-level encoder span; clip / t5 / qwen / image are nested inside it, so do not add them to 'all'.
panels.title: Conditioning encoder time p50 / p99 (ms)

panels.description: Conditioning encode time as a percent of engine time, per model. Climbing here on short requests is the signal that prompt encoding, not generation, is what the user is waiting for.
panels.title: Conditioning share of engine time (%)

panels.description: Where engine time goes: conditioning vs denoising vs VAE decode, as a percent of total engine time. Whichever band is widest is the thing to optimise. Bands will not sum to 100% on runners that cannot report every stage (Z-Image-Turbo reports only the total).
panels.title: Engine time split: conditioning vs denoising vs VAE decode (%)

panels.description: Model inference p95 broken down by device_id. For sp_runner (multihost video) each host emits its own time series via TT_VISIBLE_DEVICES. Diverging lines = a slow host (straggler).
panels.title: Inference p95 by device_id

panels.description: Successful model inferences per second per device_id. Tells you how throughput is distributed across hosts.
panels.title: Inferences/sec by device_id (success only)

panels.description: Heatmap of model inference latency. Each row is a latency bucket; intensity = count. Reveals bimodal distributions and tail latency growth that quantiles can hide.
panels.title: Inference Latency Heatmap

panels.description: Inference success vs failure rate per device_id. A device with rising failures while others are healthy is a host issue, not a model issue.
panels.title: Inference success vs failure by device_id

panels.description: Cross-host inference p95 skew: max(device_id) - min(device_id). Spikes here mean one host is much slower than the others (straggler detection for multihost video gen).

targets.expr: max(histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (device_id, le) (rate(tt_media_server_model_inference_duration_seconds_bucket{service=~"$service",model_type=~"$model_type",device_id=~"$device_id"}[5m])))) - min(histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (device_id, le) (rate(tt_media_server_model_inference_duration_seconds_bucket{service=~"$service",model_type=~"$model_type",device_id=~"$device_id"}[5m]))))

panels.title: Cross-host p95 skew (straggler detector)

panels.description: Device warmup p95 per device_id. Warmup happens once at startup; long warmup on a single device usually means a slow weight load on that host.
panels.title: Device warmup p95 per device

panels.description: Cumulative device warmup attempts split by status. Persistent failures here block a host from accepting traffic.
panels.title: Warmup totals by device / status

panels.description: Cumulative model load operations split by status. Should stay flat after startup; spikes mean reloads.
panels.title: Model load totals by device / status

panels.description: Result download success vs failure rate. Failures here usually mean object store / network problems, not model problems.
panels.title: Download result rate (success / failure)

panels.description: Result download p95 duration per model_type.
panels.title: Download result p95 duration

panels.description: CPU % consumed by Python tt-media-server processes (uvicorn parent + workers). Sourced from process-exporter group `tt_media_server_python` (see process-exporter.yml).
panels.title: CPU % (Python processes)

panels.description: Resident set size in MB across all Python tt-media-server processes.
panels.title: Memory RSS (MB)

panels.description: Total threads across Python tt-media-server processes.
panels.title: Threads

panels.description: Open file descriptors. Steady growth = leak suspect.
panels.title: Open file descriptors

panels.description: Number of distinct uvicorn / Python worker processes. Verifies your worker fan-out matches the configured count.
panels.title: Process count

panels.description: Major + minor page faults / sec. Sustained majors = thrashing or memory-mapped IO pressure.
panels.title: Page faults / sec

panels.description: System info reported by the server at startup (version, environment, device_mesh_shape, model_runner).
panels.title: Server info

title: TT Media Server (Python)
